# pbwire

> pbwire is a dynamic Protobuf runtime for C. It loads a schema at runtime — a hand-built descriptor
> tree or a standard `FileDescriptorSet` — then builds, reads, encodes and decodes messages through
> reflection, speaking the standard Protobuf binary wire format plus the JSON mapping and the text
> format. No code generation, no `protoc` at runtime, no libprotobuf in the process: C99, one public
> header, about 10k lines of C, zero runtime dependencies.

Facts: source at <https://github.com/jinganix/pbwire>, license Apache-2.0, version `0.1.0`
(`project(pbwire VERSION ...)` in `CMakeLists.txt`). Encodings are byte-identical to `protoc 36.2`
and pass Google's official conformance suites: binary + JSON 2745 successes, 0 skipped (2 expected
failures that the reference C++ testee fails identically:
`Required.Proto2/Proto3.ProtobufInput.BadTag_FieldNumberSlightlyTooHigh`; pbwire additionally
passes 4 JSON tests the reference fails, `SingleValueForRepeatedFieldInt32/Message` on both
syntaxes) and text 445 successes with 0 failures — including 4 the reference itself fails
(bad-UTF-8 strings, `\U` past the planes).
Requirements: a C99 compiler for the core;
CMake + C++17 + libprotobuf only for the optional `.proto` importer `pbwire-protoc`.

## Build and test

```bash
make              # build/libpbwire.a
make test         # core + threads + descriptor-set self-checks (required before commit)
make format       # clang-format >= 19; make format-check for the gate

cmake -B build-cmake && cmake --build build-cmake && (cd build-cmake && ctest)
cmake -B build-cmake -DPBW_BUILD_PROTOC=ON   # adds the .proto importer (needs libprotobuf)
```

Optional, needs `protoc` + libprotobuf C++: `make difftest` (differential test against the official
C++ runtime), `make bench`. Optional, needs a protobuf v36.2 source checkout:
`PBWIRE_PROTOBUF_SRC=$PWD/protobuf make conformance`.

## API

- `pbw_schema *pbw_schema_new(void)` / `pbw_schema_free(pbw_schema *)`
- `pbw_descriptor *pbw_schema_add_message(pbw_schema *, const char *name)`, `pbw_schema_add_enum`,
  `pbw_schema_find(const pbw_schema *, const char *name)`; `pbw_schema_link()` resolves type names.
- `pbw_field *pbw_message_add_field(pbw_descriptor *msg, const char *name, uint32_t number,
  pbw_type type, pbw_label label)`; `pbw_message_add_extension` (same, but only the number must
  be unique); `pbw_field_set_type_name`, `pbw_field_set_packed`, `pbw_field_set_oneof`;
  `pbw_field_default_value`, `pbw_field_is_extension`.
- `pbw_status pbw_descriptor_set_load(const void *data, size_t len, pbw_schema **out)`: standard
  `FileDescriptorSet` -> linked schema; `pbw_schema_error()` explains a failure.
- `pbw_message *pbw_message_new(const pbw_descriptor *)`, `pbw_message_free`;
  `pbw_message_is_initialized` (proto2 `required` check; `pbw_decode` already enforces it);
  `pbw_message_set(pbw_message *, uint32_t number, pbw_value *)` takes ownership of the value on
  success only; `pbw_message_get`, `pbw_message_clear`, `pbw_message_set_message`.
- `pbw_value_new_{int,uint,bool,float,double,string,bytes,message}`, typed getters
  (`pbw_value_get_int32`, `pbw_value_get_string`, ...), repeated access with `pbw_value_count` /
  `pbw_value_at`.
- `pbw_status pbw_encode(const pbw_message *, uint8_t **out, size_t *len)` ->
  `pbw_free()`; `pbw_status pbw_decode(const pbw_descriptor *, const void *buf, size_t len,
  pbw_message **out)` -> `pbw_message_free()`.
- `pbw_ctx *pbw_ctx_new(void)`: one arena + encode buffer per thread; `pbw_decode_ctx`,
  `pbw_encode_ctx`, `pbw_ctx_reset` (frees the whole tree at once), `pbw_ctx_used`, `pbw_ctx_free`,
  `pbw_ctx_set_retain_cap` (resident budget across resets, default 1 MiB, 0 keeps nothing),
  `pbw_pool_*` (bounded freelist: acquire/release/idle, one pool per worker, no locks).
- `pbw_limits { max_bytes, max_depth }` (0 = default) with `pbw_decode_limits` and
  `pbw_decode_ctx_limits`; over-large `max_depth` clamps to `PBW_MAX_DEPTH`.
- `pbw_encode_deterministic`: map entries sorted by key, everything else byte-identical to
  `pbw_encode`.
- Streaming: `pbw_encode_delimited` (varint length + message), `pbw_istream_new/feed/next/reset/free`
  (`*out == NULL` + `PBW_OK` means need more data), `pbw_encode_sink(msg, sink, opaque)` in 8 KiB
  chunks with a `pbw_status`-returning sink.
- `PBW_ABI_VERSION` (== 1) with `pbw_abi_version()`; the shared library SONAME carries the same
  number. Additive C API changes keep it; breaking changes bump it and the SONAME together.

## Key facts

- Explicit presence: a field absent on the wire stays absent; no defaults are filled in.
- Dialect per descriptor, from the file it came from (hand-built schemas default to proto3;
  `pbw_schema_set_proto3(schema, 0)` gives proto2). A proto2 closed enum's unknown number is kept as
  an unknown field instead of the field value, also inside packed repetition. A proto2 `required`
  field is rejected by `pbw_decode()` (`PBW_ERR_REQUIRED`) and reported by
  `pbw_message_is_initialized()`; `pbw_encode()` writes the tree as it stands, like the reference
  serializer.
- Wire data is untrusted input: lengths bounds-checked, field number 0 and wire types above 5
  rejected, nesting capped at 100 (`PBW_MAX_DEPTH`), every failure returns a `pbw_status`.
- Descriptors are trusted input; loading adversarial descriptor sets is out of scope.
- Dynamic schema loading: `pbw_descriptor_set_load()` reads a standard `FileDescriptorSet` produced by
  `protoc --include_imports --descriptor_set_out`, `buf build -o`, or the optional `pbwire-protoc`
  library. Every imported file must be in the set (types resolve by name), otherwise the load fails
  with `unknown type ... for field ...` in `pbw_schema_error()`. The loader reads names, numbers,
  types, labels, oneofs, `packed`, defaults and the file syntax, plus extensions with their
  extendee; services, reserved ranges and source info are ignored. proto3/edition-2023 sets get
  packed repetition by default.
- The schema owns its descriptors and must outlive every message, value and `pbw_ctx` tree built from
  it; treat a linked schema as read-only while other threads use it.
- Unknown fields (including a known field with the wrong wire type) are preserved as raw wire bytes
  and re-emitted after the known fields, in input order.
- No globals and no thread-local state: confine a schema or message to one thread. `pbw_ctx` gives
  arena and encode-buffer reuse per thread; messages decoded through a context are read-only and
  freed by `pbw_ctx_reset`. `pbw_ctx_set_retain_cap` bounds the resident bytes without adding
  shared state.
- `tests/test_threads.c` is the multi-thread gate: shared linked schema reflection, one `pbw_ctx`
  per thread, plain per-message ownership, per-thread `pbw_descriptor_set_load()` of the same bytes
  (including the truncated-set error path), one shared loaded schema for decode/encode, and a
  1-vs-8-thread throughput comparison that fails if aggregate throughput collapses. `make bench`
  prints the same comparison per implementation next to the generated-code rows.
- `pbw_decode()` gives every decoded tree its own arena (one `malloc` for the whole tree), so
  `pbw_message_free()` releases subtrees, values and payloads at once: values taken from a decoded
  message are not individually freeable, and the tree is still mutable (`pbw_message_set`,
  `pbw_message_clear`, `pbw_message_set_message` work on it).
- Two allocation strategies, same bytes: `pbw_ctx` (`pbw_decode_ctx`/`pbw_encode_ctx`) reuses one
  arena and one output buffer, so a steady loop stops calling `malloc`; its messages are read-only
  and die with `pbw_ctx_reset`. The plain `pbw_decode`/`pbw_encode` allocate one tree and one buffer
  per call, the caller owns both (`pbw_message_free`/`pbw_free`), and the tree is mutable. Use the
  context in hot loops and per worker thread, the plain API for one-off or long-lived results.
- Numbers are raw bit patterns; the descriptor type decides which typed getter applies. Repeated
  numeric fields accept both packed and unpacked encodings; the descriptor controls encoding, and
  proto3 schemas loaded from a `FileDescriptorSet` get packed defaults.
- Two independent libraries in one repository: `pbwire` (pure C, no dependency) and
  `pbwire-protoc` (C++17 + libprotobuf, `.proto` -> `FileDescriptorSet`). They meet only at the
  serialized descriptor set.
- ABI stability: `PBW_ABI_VERSION` in the header, `pbw_abi_version()` at runtime, CMake
  `SOVERSION 1`, `make shared` producing `libpbwire.so.1` / `libpbwire.1.dylib`. Additive changes
  keep the number, breaking changes bump it with the SONAME. `bindings/python` (cffi, ABI mode)
  and `bindings/go/pbwire` (cgo) pin it at load and round-trip scalar messages.
- Not implemented: RPC/HTTP, MessageSet decoding into extensions, code generation.
- Text format (`pbw_text_print` / `pbw_text_parse`): printer output is byte-identical to the
  reference; the parser matches it (extensions as `[full.name]`, group type names, `Any`
  expansions, unknown fields as numeric lines with `print_unknown_fields`, strict rejections
  including bad-UTF-8 strings, singular duplicates and unknown names).
- JSON mapping (`pbw_json_print` / `pbw_json_parse`): same verdicts as the reference parser on
  40,000 mutated inputs; all well-known types (`Any`, `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `FieldMask`,
  `Struct`/`Value`, wrappers, `Empty`), extensions as `[full.name]`, closed-enum unknowns kept as
  unknown fields, strict base64 (padded input must fill quanta) and strict numbers.

## Optional

- [tests/test_pbwire.c](tests/test_pbwire.c): golden `protoc 36.2` bytes and edge cases, usable as
  executable examples.
- [bench/bench.cc](bench/bench.cc): differential test and benchmark against libprotobuf C++
  (generated code and `DynamicMessage`).
- [conformance/testee.c](conformance/testee.c): testee for Google's `conformance_test_runner`, binary
  wire format only.
